intro: This tree shows how the roughly 150 accepted genera of the arum family are grouped: first into subfamilies, then into tribes, and finally into the genera themselves.

Its backbone comes from The Genera of Araceae (Mayo, Bogner and Boyce, Kew, 1997), still the only work that places every genus in a tribe. Where later research has changed that picture, the tree follows the later research.

currentWith.heading: Brought up to date with the 2022 phylogenomic study
currentWith.body: The most recent family-wide study (Haigh and colleagues, 2022, American Journal of Botany) sequenced 128 species across 111 genera. Its conclusions are applied here, not just noted:
applied: Calla now sits inside Aroideae. The old subfamily Calloideae is not used.
Zamioculcadoideae is treated as part of Aroideae.
The duckweeds are included as subfamily Lemnoideae — they were still a separate family in 1997.
Lasioideae is divided into two tribes, Lasieae and Dracontieae.
The tribe Aglaonemateae holds Aglaonema and Boycea.
unresolved: Where subfamily Lasioideae attaches to the rest of the family is still unsettled.
The positions of Montrichardia, Zantedeschia and Anchomanes are only moderately supported.

uncertainty.heading: Why some branches are dashed
uncertainty.body: A dashed branch means the genus was named, revived or moved after 1997 and no study we hold places it in a tribe outright. Its position is our best reading of the literature rather than a published conclusion, and it is drawn differently so you can tell the two apart. Every other genus here sits where a named source puts it.

counts.heading: Where the numbers come from
counts.body: Species totals follow Kew's Plants of the World Online and count formally described species. Aroidpedia's own pages often list more, because the archive covers plants that have not been described yet.

reading.heading: Reading the tree
reading.body: Colour marks the level: family, subfamily, tribe, genus. A branch takes the colour of whatever it leads to, so you can follow a lineage down by shade alone. Selecting a genus lights its whole line back to the family.

provenance.ranges: Native-range buckets parsed 2026-08-07 from the POWO genus exports' GEOGRAPHY prose (Araceae_Exports/EXCELS), species rows only, hybrids excluded. Zones NW/AF/EU-WAsia/AS/AU; a zone under 5% of a genus's mentions is trace and ignored; NW+OW=worldwide, several OW zones need a 66% leader or the genus is oldworld. Pseudodracontium (Indo-China) and Pedicellarum (Borneo) hand-set: no workbook in the export; both ranges are uncontested. 1.8.0 adds range.places: the distinct POWO base names per genus, most-mentioned first, INCLUDING the parenthesised sub-units (Borneo (Sarawak) yields both) - zones still count the outer name only. Hand-set places for the two workbook-less genera.
